title: Bug:Race condition causes `CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED` to be set to 0 causing swss start to fail
author: gpunathilell
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug


On a **smart switch** (NPU plus one or more DPUs), SONiC runs **several database Docker instances**: the main **`database`** service and per-DPU instances such as **`database@dpu0`**, **`database@dpu1`**, and so on. Each instance is brought up through the same overall pattern: **systemd** runs **`/usr/local/bin/database.sh`**, which delegates to **`/usr/bin/database.sh`** — the script generated from **`docker_image_ctl.j2`** for the database image.

During container start, that generated script updates the host indicator **`CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED`** in **host `CONFIG_DB`**. For DPU database instances, the CLI path still targets the **same** host `CONFIG_DB` Redis as the NPU (not an isolated DB per DPU for this key). As a result, **every** database instance that executes the initialization block can **`SET`** the same key, often toggling **`0`** and later **`1`**, depending on whether first-boot pending configuration is present and which branch of the script runs.

**`config-setup.service`** runs in parallel with early container bring-up on boot. Near the end of first-time (or factory) configuration it removes **`/tmp/pending_config_initialization`** and sets **`CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED`** to **`1`** after loading configuration (for example via **`config reload`**). Because **`config-setup`** can **finish** (systemd reports the unit complete) in the **same narrow time window** as **`database@dpu*`** units still running their **`docker_image_ctl`** start logic, another database instance can still run the branch that **`SET`s `CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED` to `0`** on the host after **`config-setup`** has already set **`1`**. There is a short window where the value is wrong, or, if the script does not reach the final **`SET 1`**, the key can remain **`0`**.

**`swss`** (and related start logic) **waits for `CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED` to become `1`** before proceeding. If it observes **`0`** during that wait, or startup ordering is unlucky, **`swss`** can hit **start-pre timeouts** or otherwise fail to start cleanly even though configuration was applied successfully — a failure mode that presents as **`swss` not coming up** rather than as a clear configuration error.

In short: **multiple writers** on a **single** host key, **non-deterministic** completion order across **`config-setup`** and **`database` / `database@dpu*`**, and **`swss`** blocking on that key combine into a **race** that is especially plausible on smart-switch images with several database instances.


### Steps to Reproduce

Reproduce on a **smart-switch** SKU where **`database.service`** and **`database@dpu*`** units are all enabled, using a boot path that **creates** **`/tmp/pending_config_initialization`** and runs **full first-boot configuration** (for example **factory default**, **ZTP**, runs **`config-setup`** and **`config reload`** while containers are starting).

Power-cycle or cold-boot the system (or otherwise run a **first boot** where **`config-setup`** and **all database instances** start together). The race is timing-dependent: it may not trigger on every boot, but it becomes more likely when **many DPU database containers** start close to **`config-setup`** completion and each executes the **`CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED`** logic against **host `CONFIG_DB`**.

Collecting **ordered logs** for **`config-setup`**, **`database`**, **`database@dpu*`**, and **`swss`**, and optionally sampling **`sonic-db-cli CONFIG_DB GET CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED`** during the first minute after boot, helps confirm the overlap when the issue appears.


### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

- **`CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED`** on **host `CONFIG_DB`** may be **written multiple times** by **different** database **`docker_image_ctl`** start paths (main **`database`** plus **`dpu*`** instances), not only by **`config-setup`** / **`config reload`**.
- Around **`config-setup`** completion, the key can momentarily go to **`0`** again or stay **`0`** if a later writer’s sequence does not complete as intended.
- **`swss`** may **block or time out** in **start-pre** waiting for initialization, leading to **service start failure** or delayed dataplane bring-up even when the underlying config load succeeded.

**Expected Behavior**
- **`swss`** should reliably observe **`CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED == 1`** once configuration is valid, and **start** without spurious **timeouts** caused by **cross-instance** writes to the same key.

2026-04-09T02:45:26.662945+00:00 sonic systemd[1]: Finished config-setup.service - Config initialization and migration service.
2026-04-09T02:45:26.673736+00:00 sonic root: Started databasedpu0 service...

2026-04-09T02:45:26.674022+00:00 sonic root: Started databasedpu3 service...

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/26748

#### Why I did it

DPU database instances must not touch the host CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED flag. Only the main NPU database instance should manage this key to avoid a race where DPU instances overwrite CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED back to 0 after config-setup has already set it to 1, causing swss startup to fail.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Added a gate for `$DATABASE_TYPE` before CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED is set in docker postStartAction(). CONFIG_DB_INITIALIZED is allowed to be touched only if `$DATABASE_TYPE` is not `dpudb`.

#### How to verify it

 - Make sure first boot of a new image with the fix proceeds successfully with all critical containers including swss coming up on the NPU.
 - Cold boot a smartswitch multiple times with the fix and make sure that all critical containers including swss come up on the NPU.
